requirement:
After one valid judgment, the harness MUST write the subject text, submitted
determination and rationale, and recorded inputs using the existing evidence
schema. {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`
By default, it MUST write the subject's evidence file. With `--stdout`, it MUST
emit a single evidence JSON object followed by a newline to stdout and MUST NOT
create or change evidence files or directories. All three outcomes MUST be
written to the selected destination as completed assessments; their validation
status MUST follow {cite}`requirements.ci.determination`.
rationale:
## Obligations and coverage

- **After a valid judgment, persist the subject text, determination, rationale, and recorded inputs using the existing schema.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[assess]` obtains the accepted judgment and builds the record through `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[record]`. Its definition branch supplies the subject text, reference digest, rationale, determination, and recorded inputs. `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[recorded_inputs]` passes through the recorded inputs. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` asserts the text, submitted outcome and rationale, exact record keys, and the presence of requirements, definition, and outline inputs; it also checks that outline inputs contain only file, selector, and hash. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[false_is_a_completed_assessment]` checks the persisted file's rationale and recorded inputs, including absence of outline source text.
- **By default, write the subject's evidence file.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#impl[AuthoringSubject]/fn[evidence_path]` selects the definition evidence path. `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_assessment]` creates the parent and writes the JSON in file mode; `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[write_record]` writes batch records by complete-file replacement. The default destination is exercised by `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[false_is_a_completed_assessment]` and `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs]`; batch persistence is exercised by `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[terminal_progress_distinguishes_judgments_from_authoring_errors]` and `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[a_denied_mandatory_input_aborts_only_its_assessment]`.
- **With `--stdout`, emit one evidence JSON object and a trailing newline.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_assessment]` serializes one record, appends a newline, and writes it to stdout. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` parses the entire stdout as one object and asserts its final newline, covering all three outcomes and verbose/default reporting paths.
- **With `--stdout`, neither create nor change evidence files or directories.** The stdout branch performs no evidence-path creation or file write. The same test checks unchanged existing evidence and, separately, that an absent evidence directory remains absent.
- **Write true, false, and FIXME to the selected destination as completed assessments.** `src/judgment.rs#impl[Judgment]/fn[to_value]` encodes all three outcomes without treating false or FIXME as authoring errors. `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_assessment]` writes them through the same destination branches, and `src/authoring/mod.rs#impl[PendingAssessment]/fn[persisted]` completes persisted batch assessments. The stdout test checks all three recorded outcomes and completed usage status; the false-assessment test checks completed file-mode usage; the batch tests assert persisted true, false, and FIXME results.
- **Preserve the validation status specified by `requirements.ci.determination`.** The harness records the actual outcome using `Judgment::to_value`, rather than converting negative judgments into success or authoring failures. The three-outcome stdout assertions verify this application of the cited requirement. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[false_is_a_completed_assessment]` additionally runs repository validation and asserts that the persisted false outcome fails with its rationale. The cited validator's own implementation and broader test coverage are not reassessed here.

No unmet obligation or unacknowledged gap was found.

text: :::{req} persistence
After one valid judgment, the harness MUST write the subject text, submitted
determination and rationale, and recorded inputs using the existing evidence
schema. {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`
By default, it MUST write the subject's evidence file. With `--stdout`, it MUST
emit a single evidence JSON object followed by a newline to stdout and MUST NOT
create or change evidence files or directories. All three outcomes MUST be
written to the selected destination as completed assessments; their validation
status MUST follow {cite}`requirements.ci.determination`.
:::{req} schema

A requirement or example evidence file at `evidence/<full-name>.json` MUST be a JSON object with exactly `requirement` or `example`, `determination`, `rationale`, `references`, and `inputs`. `references` MUST be the reference-set digest defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`. The definition text and rationale MUST be nonempty strings, `determination` MUST use one of the outcomes defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`, and `inputs` MUST be an array. Every evidence input MUST have exactly one of three forms: an outline input with `file`, `item`, and `hash`; a requirements input with `requirements`, `matches`, and `text`; or a definition input with `definition` and `text`. File paths MUST resolve to permitted inputs under {cite}`requirements.ci.input_containment`. Project-local paths SHOULD be recorded relative to the project for portability; absolute and parent-relative paths MAY be used when their resolved targets are permitted. `matches` MUST be an array of distinct full definition names, `hash` MUST be a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, and `text` MUST be a nonempty array of strings. Evidence MUST NOT store source text for outline inputs.
:::{req} determination

For requirement and example evidence, both `true` and `FIXME` MUST satisfy the determination check in `habeas::validate()`. A false determination MUST fail validation and be reported with its rationale. Each definition's determination MUST be checked on its own; a false determination MUST NOT fail the definitions it implements, tests, or cites. All other evidence checks MUST still pass: FIXME MUST NOT excuse malformed, missing, or stale evidence or uncovered references. Validation MUST check the recorded outcome, schema, input freshness, and reference coverage without inference or reassessing whether a source comment adequately acknowledges a gap.
:::{req} policy
Every `habeas author` form MUST assess its subjects under an assessment policy,
`confirm` or `once`. The policy MUST come from `--policy <name>` when given,
otherwise from the selected configuration's `policy`, and otherwise MUST be
`confirm`. Under `confirm`, each subject MUST be assessed as
{cite}`requirements.authoring.confirmation` specifies. Under `once`, each subject
MUST receive a single assessment, whose result is recorded; it uses fewer tokens
and less time, such as with a slow local model. An unknown policy name MUST be
rejected as invalid configuration or arguments. The completion report MUST name
the policy used, and each usage record MUST identify it.
